Questions

How many grams is a stick of butter?

One US stick is 4 oz: 113 g, 8 tablespoons, or 1/2 cup.

Why do I see 113 g, 113.5 g and 227 g?

A stick is 4 oz, which works out to 113.4 g. A cup is 2 sticks, 226.8 g. USDA FoodData Central and the King Arthur chart round those to 113 g and 227 g. Half of 227 g is 113.5 g, which is why some charts list 113.5.

How many sticks is a 250 g block?

About 2.20 sticks: 2 sticks plus 23 g. Use that as an example only. Package sizes were not checked.

Does choosing a metric cup change a stick?

No. A stick stays 4 oz. The cup size is the only thing that changes.

Is a scale more accurate?

Yes. Weigh the butter when you can. A spoon measure is a kitchen estimate.

Where the numbers come from

1 oz = 28.349523125 g. This page rounds 4 oz values to whole grams: 113 g for a stick, 227 g for a cup, and 14 g for a tablespoon. Those whole-gram figures match both sources below.

U.S. Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service. FoodData Central. Butter, salted, FDC 173410: stick 113 g, tablespoon 14.2 g, cup 227 g.

King Arthur Baking Ingredient Weight Chart: butter, 8 tablespoons (1/2 cup) = 4 oz = 113 g.

What this does not cover

This page does not cover melted, whipped, or plant-based butter. Salted and unsalted weight differences were not checked, and butter package sizes outside the US were not checked.

It is a kitchen estimate. A scale is the most accurate.
